title: Things to do in Padua: 5 places and how to plan your visits
description: Visit five places in Padua: Scrovegni, Palazzo della Ragione, Saint Anthony’s Basilica, the Botanical Garden and Prato, with booking and November 2026 closure advice.
intro: Padua, called Padova in Italian, combines painting, architecture, plants and everyday life in its squares. Five places make a useful starting selection: the Scrovegni Chapel, Palazzo della Ragione, the Basilica of Saint Anthony, the Botanical Garden and Prato della Valle. Plan the admissions that determine your day first, then connect the stops through the centre. That leaves room to appreciate the city instead of simply collecting entry tickets.

November 2026 notice: the official Scrovegni website announces that the chapel will close from 16 to 27 November for fresco inspections. This information was checked on 8 November. If your trip falls within that period, do not organize it around an unavailable admission. Choose the other four places and consult the operator for renewed availability. The guide below explains which stops require booking, how their access conditions differ and how to adapt the route.

sections.heading: 1. Scrovegni Chapel: make this your first booking decision
paragraphs: The chapel is a reason to visit Padua for art. Giotto painted its fresco cycle in 1303–1305, combining scenes from the lives of Mary and Christ, allegories and the Last Judgement beneath a star-filled blue vault. Learn that broad arrangement before entering so that you can approach the pictures as a connected narrative. Recognizing every scene is unnecessary; selecting a few and relating them to the whole is often more useful than rushing through a list of famous images.

The tourist office requires booking at least one day in advance and warns that late arrival can prevent admission. The operator confirms that same-day reservations cannot be made. Save the instructions accompanying your purchase and allow enough time for ticket collection and the access procedure. Do not plan a train that arrives at the moment your visit begins. The announced closure on 16–27 November 2026 takes precedence over general opening information. Seeing the exterior does not give you a view of the frescoes, so recognize that limitation if admission is unavailable.

sections.heading: 2. Palazzo della Ragione: distinguish the hall from the market
paragraphs: Palazzo della Ragione stands among the central squares and has a history reaching back to the thirteenth century. Tourism information highlights its large elevated hall and medieval astrological fresco cycle, alongside the wooden horse and other features that help explain the building’s uses and meanings. Going inside reveals why this is more than a backdrop for café terraces. It is a particularly useful cultural stop if you are interested in depictions of time and the organization of urban life.

The food shops of the Sotto il Salone market are below, while the visitable hall is upstairs. Browsing the shops is different from entering to see the paintings, and a hall ticket does not guarantee that every shop will be trading. The operator identifies Piazza delle Erbe as the palace address and lists an entrance for visitors with physical disabilities through the municipal courtyard on Via 8 Febbraio. Confirm the availability of that route if you depend on it, rather than automatically following other visitors up a staircase.

sections.heading: 3. Basilica of Saint Anthony: art within an active pilgrimage site
paragraphs: The Basilica of Saint Anthony, known locally as Il Santo, combines artistic interest with an active religious role. The official tourism route places it on Piazza del Santo and emphasizes its pilgrimage tradition. Start outside with the façade, domes and square; Donatello’s equestrian monument to Gattamelata is also here. Then consider how to visit the interior respectfully around the activities taking place in the church.

The official regulations specify free entry to the basilica during its opening hours, suitable clothing, silenced devices and a prohibition on photographic equipment. The exterior photograph in this guide does not establish permission to take photographs inside. Nor should free basilica admission be extended to associated museums or other spaces, which may have separate conditions. For reduced mobility, the operator identifies the central door as the entrance and lists accessible toilets in the Blessed Luca Belludi Cloister. Reconfirm practical arrangements before a visit that depends on those facilities.

sections.heading: 4. Botanical Garden: compare the historic garden and biodiversity spaces
paragraphs: The University of Padua’s Botanical Garden was established in 1545 and inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1997. It offers a change of pace with a scientific purpose, rooted in research and teaching. A visit combines the older garden with the later biodiversity development. Look at how plants are organized and how the historic spaces differ from the recreated environments. That contrast tells you more about the place than a sequence of flower photographs without explanation.

The garden lies between Prato della Valle and the basilica, making it a convenient part of the same section of your outing. The operator accepts printed tickets or tickets displayed on a device and explains that presale charges depend on the product. Its listed QR audioguide is available in Italian, English and German. Bring a charged phone and your own headphones if you plan to use it. Consult the current calendar carefully: the opening-times page mixes exceptions dated in different years, so older holiday arrangements should not be transferred automatically to a 2026 visit.

sections.heading: 5. Prato della Valle: finish with a square worth walking around
paragraphs: Prato della Valle offers something different from the indoor stops. Its layout revolves around a central island, canal, bridges and statues. Tourism Padova describes 78 sculptures and four bridges. Instead of pursuing an uncertain ranking among Europe’s largest squares, follow one side of the canal and notice how the perspective changes between water, monuments and surrounding façades. The layout itself provides a reason to explore rather than simply stop at its edge.

This is a useful place to slow down after several visits. If you want photographs of reflections or sculptural details, choose a position on the walkway and leave room for other people to pass. You do not need a market or event to make the stop worthwhile. Any such calendar should be checked separately, rather than inferred from an archive image. From here you can organize your return or head towards your accommodation. Leave time for that final journey: finishing a circuit of the square does not mean you have already reached the railway station.

sections.heading: Reservations, Mondays and comparing ticket combinations
paragraphs: A useful purchase order is to check Scrovegni first, then decide whether you want to enter Palazzo della Ragione and the Botanical Garden. Operators have different terms and possible combinations. Before buying a city card or combined ticket, list the places you will actually visit and establish whether the particular reservation you need is included. General coverage does not guarantee space at your preferred time. Avoid overlapping purchases simply because the same museum names appear in more than one offer.

The Palazzo della Ragione operator lists Tuesday–Sunday opening and a normal Monday closure, with public-holiday exceptions. That rule should not be applied to every attraction in Padua. For the garden, check its current calendar and notices for your specific date; for the basilica, review worship and access times. Admission categories can depend on age, residence, services and presale fees. This route therefore assumes neither a universal price nor that free church entry makes the entire day free.

sections.heading: Arrive by train and adapt the walk to your needs
paragraphs: When searching trains from Venice or another city, use Padova as the destination and confirm the service, departure station and ticket for your date. Tourism information describes the station’s connection to the centre along Corso del Popolo, alongside bus and tram options. Do not treat an old timetable on an information page as a guaranteed departure today. Consult the transport operator for the specific service and allow a buffer between arrival, any booked admission and the return journey.

The basilica, garden and Prato can be grouped without repeatedly moving between distant parts of the city. A walking route still requires consideration of stamina, rain, heat and level changes at each entrance. Contact venues for an accessible entrance or facilities if needed. The Venice, Verona and Bologna guides linked below help compare other stages of an Italian trip. They do not replace checking transport connections or imply that every destination works as an excursion of the same duration.

itinerary: With Scrovegni admission: organize your arrival around the confirmed slot, allowing time for its access procedure. Continue afterwards towards the central squares and Palazzo della Ragione. Plan a break before heading south rather than stringing together admissions without considering how long you want inside each building.

In the southern section, group Saint Anthony’s Basilica, the Botanical Garden and Prato della Valle. Depending on the remaining time, enter the garden or save it for another confirmed outing. Reverse the sequence when an opening time, religious service or someone’s needs make that more sensible.

Without Scrovegni availability, including during the announced November closure, give more time to the palace, basilica, garden and Prato. Staying overnight allows you to separate painting from open-air stops. The aim is to see your chosen places properly rather than force five interiors into every visit.

faq.question: Are Padua and Padova the same city?
faq.answer: Yes. Padua is the usual English name; Padova is the Italian name used on trains, maps and signs. Use Padova when checking rail connections.

faq.question: Must I book the Scrovegni Chapel?
faq.answer: Yes. The information consulted requires booking at least the day before, and the operator does not accept same-day reservations. It also announces closure on 16–27 November 2026. Check availability before committing to other services.

faq.question: Is the Basilica of Saint Anthony free to enter?
faq.answer: The regulations specify free entry to the basilica during opening hours. That does not establish the admission conditions of museums and associated spaces. Respect worship, the dress code and the ban on interior photography.

faq.question: Can I visit Padua from Venice?
faq.answer: You can plan a train outing after checking the service available for your date. Choose one main admission and a manageable route, without assuming every venue is open or that your reservation aligns with your arrival.

conclusion: Padua balances frescoes, architecture and open spaces when bookings support the route. Confirm closures before setting out and choose the interiors that matter most to you. The garden and Prato can then round out the visit without turning every stage into a race towards the next ticket desk.
